clue.text: Nervous head of royal mail again justifies letters put to one side

indicators.note: nervous means jittery and unsettled, so the letters that follow are jumbled into a new order
the head of a word is its opening letter, here taken from royal

explanation.surface: An anxious boss at the postal service once more defends setting some post aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nervous' jumbles R (from 'head of' royal) with MAIL and AGAIN. 'justifies' only joins wordplay to definition. The 'letters' are written characters in a page's margin, not post.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-style description: notes written in the margins of a book are characters placed at the edge of the page.

clue.text: Conservative garment displayed in the capital of Morocco

indicators.note: displayed in says the garment can be seen inside the name of the city that follows, once its first and last letters are set aside

parts.note: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco

explanation.surface: A Tory's outfit is put on show in a North African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed in' asks you to name the capital first, RABAT, and then look inside it. 'Conservative' is not the political party: it describes a modest, traditional robe.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by description: it is a loose, modest outer robe worn in Arab countries, hence traditional dress.

clue.text: Idiots holding small work line up? They may be moved in argument

definitions.text: They may be moved in argument

indicators.note: holding says the idiots' word has the other letters gripped inside it

parts.note: a goat is an old informal word for a fool, as in 'acting the goat'

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the three short pieces are read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Fools with a minor job stand in a queue, the sort who get shifted about in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the three short pieces upwards as LPOS, which 'holding' places within the idiots. The definition leans on the idiom for changing the terms of a dispute midway; 'line up' is not a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to shift these is to change the rules unfairly during a dispute or negotiation.

clue.text: What's possibly only OK with onset of libido?

definitions.text: What's possibly only OK with onset of libido?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the answer, together with one more letter, could be rearranged into the two words that follow
the onset of a word is its beginning, so only the opening letter of libido is used

explanation.surface: Something that is merely acceptable once desire starts to stir.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer 'with' L (from 'onset of' libido) can 'possibly' make ONLY OK. The whole clue also describes the answer, sex being welcome only when desire begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym for sexual activity, which the whole clue cheekily describes as needing desire first.

clue.text: Latin stranger is more cunning

parts.note: stranger as a comparative means more weird, more uncanny, so eerier

explanation.surface: An unfamiliar Roman turns out to be the craftier one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a noun for an unknown person, but it is the comparative adjective, more strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: leery can mean sly or knowing as well as wary, so the comparative means craftier.

clue.text: In one action plan take to arms miles away

indicators.note: to plan is to arrange or design, so as an instruction it tells you to arrange the letters that follow
away says the abbreviation for miles has gone from the words before it

explanation.surface: A single-move strategy: call troops to their weapons a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes M from TAKE TO ARMS, leaving TAKETOARS, which 'plan' (read as an instruction to arrange) rearranges. 'plan' looks like part of the definition but is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning all at once, by a single deed or blow.

clue.text: Cracks showing in retro box

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the word for box is read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: to box is to spar, to fight with the fists in practice

explanation.surface: Splits are appearing in an old-fashioned crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' turns SPAR round. 'box' is the verb for fighting, not a container, and 'Cracks' are sharp knocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb or noun: sharp knocks or blows, as in a crack on the knuckles.

clue.text: One's grabbed by silly arse in lift

indicators.note: grabbed by says the letters for one's are seized and held inside the jumbled word
silly means foolish and disordered, so the letters of the next word are muddled

parts.note: One's gives I

explanation.surface: Someone gets groped by a fool in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' makes RAE from ARSE, and 'grabbed by' puts IS inside it. 'lift' is the verb to hoist, not the British word for an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both verbs mean to move something to a higher position.

clue.text: Competitive event in which the toss takes place after the start?

definitions.text: Competitive event in which the toss takes place after the start?

parts.words: Competitive event in which the toss takes place after the start?
parts.note: sporting matches begin with the toss of a coin, but in this Shrove Tuesday contest runners flip food in a frying pan while already on the move

explanation.surface: A sporting contest where, strangely, the coin is flipped only once play has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a match where the coin toss oddly comes late. In Britain, Shrove Tuesday is marked by running contests in which each runner flips food in a frying pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Description of the British Shrove Tuesday tradition where runners flip a batter cake in a frying pan as they go.

clue.text: Main activity is abdominal surgery reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard in speech, so the phrase for abdominal surgery is taken by its sound

parts.note: the navel is the belly button, so navel is whimsically used as an adjective for the abdomen; surgery consists of operations carried out by a surgeon

explanation.surface: The hospital's chief business is said to be tummy procedures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives the sound of 'navel operations'. 'Main' is the old word for the open sea, so the definition is activity at sea, not the chief activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: the main is the sea, so this is military action carried out by a fleet.

clue.text: Pop in bar cheers mostly

parts.note: to bar is to stop, to prevent something happening

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word for cheers is used, its final letter being dropped

parts.note: cheers is British informal for goodbye, so bye

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink at the pub gets a toast, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BYE to BY. 'Pop' is a verb here (to call briefly), and 'cheers' is the casual British farewell, not a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both phrases mean to make a short casual visit.

clue.text: Note police force is on top of very large cut — there's no rush

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces named first sit above the ones named afterwards

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
the Met is the Metropolitan Police, London's police force
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very large
to pare is to cut or trim away

explanation.surface: Memo: the constabulary is handling a huge budget reduction, and nobody need hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is on top of' simply stacks the pieces in a down entry. THE MET is London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivalent expression: if you have minutes in hand, you need not hurry.

clue.text: Where you'd find lags recorded

definitions.meaning: lags are convicts in British slang, and they are found in prison, for which a slang word is the can
film-makers' phrase for footage that has been shot and stored in its tin

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for being in jail, and the film-industry idiom for footage already shot and finished.

clue.text: Rubber endlessly must erase slips

indicators.note: slips means slides out of place, so the letters before it shift into a new order
endlessly means without ends, so each of the two words loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An eraser has to wipe out mistakes without ever stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims both words to MUS and ERAS, and 'slips' rearranges MUSERAS. 'Rubber' is not the British word for an eraser but a person who rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: someone who kneads and rubs muscles for a living is literally a person who rubs.

clue.text: No longer married, masses cite singular feelings of joy!

indicators.note: singular can mean odd or unusual, so the letters before it are put into an unusual order
no longer says the letter for married is not there any more in the words that follow

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married in genealogy

explanation.surface: Now divorced, crowds speak of remarkable happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' takes M out of MASSES CITE, leaving ASSESCITE, which 'singular' (meaning odd) rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: states of rapture or overwhelming delight.

clue.text: Colour of refurbished storey

indicators.note: to refurbish is to do something up anew, so the letters of the next word are rebuilt

explanation.surface: The paint shade of a newly done-up floor of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refurbished' rearranges STOREY; 'of' only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the name of a pale grey-white shade, like the inside of a shell.

clue.text: Top performers begin on vessels

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to begin is to start
urns are vessels, containers for tea or ashes

explanation.surface: The leading entertainers open their act aboard ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' stacks the two pieces in a down entry. 'vessels' are containers, not ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the headline acts in a show, the best entertainers on the bill.

clue.text: Secret police force succeeded in arrest

parts.note: the Stasi was the secret police of communist East Germany
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies and lists of monarchs

explanation.surface: Undercover officers managed to take someone into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only joins wordplay to definition. 'arrest' is a noun meaning a halt or stoppage, as in cardiac arrest, not a police detention.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: a stoppage or state of standstill.

clue.text: Island in the end Ronald Reagan attacked

indicators.note: something attacked is knocked about and broken up, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order
in the end points to the final letter of the word that follows, Ronald

explanation.surface: A Caribbean territory that the American president finally invaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attacked' rearranges D ('in the end' of Ronald) with REAGAN. The surface is history: President Reagan ordered the US invasion of this Caribbean island in 1983.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a Caribbean nation in the Windward chain.

clue.text: Nice rag flourished for straight sort of nose

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective that names this kind of nose, one running straight down from the forehead

indicators.note: to flourish something is to wave it about, so the letters before it are waved into a new order

explanation.surface: A fine handkerchief is waved about for a well-shaped conk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourished' rearranges NICE RAG; 'for' joins wordplay to definition. The answer is the adjective that labels this profile.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive label: a nose with no dip at the bridge, as on classical Greek statues, is called this.

clue.text: Judge set out to get one assistant

indicators.note: out can mean astray or wrong, so the letters of the word before it are disordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a mate is a helper to a skilled worker, as in a plumber's mate

explanation.surface: A magistrate went looking to hire a single helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns SET into EST; 'to get' just joins the pieces. 'Judge' is a verb here, to gauge roughly, not a person in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to gauge or reckon a value roughly.

clue.text: What bride says about a husband in a state

indicators.note: about says the bride's words go around the two letters that follow

parts.note: I do is the bride's reply in the wedding vows
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

explanation.surface: A woman's wedding-day words concerning her new spouse, who is in a real mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps I DO round A and H; 'in' joins wordplay to definition. 'a state' is one of the United States, not a flustered condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is one of the fifty United States, in the north-west.

clue.text: Rat that's seen on dam in Europe

indicators.note: seen on asks what stands attached to the front of the word dam in a place name, leaving that part alone

parts.note: Rotterdam is a major port city in Europe, in the Netherlands

explanation.surface: A rodent spotted on a river barrier somewhere on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen on dam' asks what is attached to DAM in the name of a European city, Rotterdam. The 'Rat' is a despicable person, not a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: old-fashioned British slang for a cad or scoundrel.

clue.text: True change of direction upfront for William, say

indicators.note: the direction at the front of the word, left, is switched to the opposite one, right

parts.note: true means faithful, so loyal
L is the abbreviation for left, a direction
R is the abbreviation for right, the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A genuine swerve by the forwards on behalf of a man called William, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of direction upfront' swaps the opening L (left) of LOYAL for R (right). Prince William is an example of the definition, flagged by 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Prince William is a member of Britain's reigning family, so he is one of these.

clue.text: Potential chancellor once a fellow good at planning growth

definitions.text: a fellow good at planning growth

parts.note: potential as a noun means capability, what someone is able to do
Gordon Brown was Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer, its finance minister, from 1997 to 2007

explanation.surface: A possible future finance minister was formerly a chap skilled in economic strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'growth' is of plants, not the economy: this was the nickname of Lancelot Brown, the 18th-century English landscape gardener who designed great country-house parks.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: he was the famous 18th-century English landscape gardener, who laid out parks of trees and lawns.

clue.text: River's character mentioned

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', leaving a river as the thing defined

indicators.note: mentioned means said in speech, so the name of the letter is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a character is a letter of the alphabet, here Y

explanation.surface: The nature of a waterway comes up in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned' gives the spoken name of the letter Y. 'character' is a letter, not a personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a waterway running along the border of England and Wales.

clue.text: Art's partner has last month off initially

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the final month of the year

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word before it, off, is taken

explanation.surface: Arthur's other half had the previous four weeks away from work at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes O from 'off'; 'has' joins the pieces. 'Art' is not a man's name: the definition wants the word paired with it in the name of the 1920s design style.
explanation.definitionFit: Collocation: the word that follows 'Art' in the name of the 1920s and 1930s decorative style.

clue.text: Shades of celebrated young women

parts.note: to sing someone's praises is to celebrate them, so celebrated gives sung
lasses are girls or young women, especially in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: The ghosts of famous girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins definition to wordplay. 'Shades' is informal for dark glasses, not ghosts or hues.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: dark spectacles worn against bright light.
